data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Internal redundancy is strictly worse for correlated failure because the act of building internal redundancy often creates homogeneity, which is the very vector for correlated failure; decentralized networks, by definition, are built on heterogeneity.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the large service intentionally uses diverse redundancy (e.g., different OS versions, different hardware vendors).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decentralized network, despite different operators, uses identical open-source software stacks.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Homogeneity Tax: To build internal redundancy efficiently, engineers replicate the same component (e.g., 10 identical servers with the same OS). This homogeneity is efficient for load balancing but maximizes correlated failure risk. If one server fails due to a memory leak under a specific load, all will. Decentralization implies different operators, which implies different choices, creating heterogeneity. This heterogeneity is the direct mechanism of resilience, not the network topology itself.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
